messages:
maria: Noticing a subtle correctness regression in Caspian's LoRA merge when running int4 quant. Some customers see their currency strings lose separators and switch to verbose units. Need quick triage.

dan: Can you paste the failing examples and which quant stack was used? GPTQ or AWQ?

maria: AWQ-4bit (default pipeline) + tokenizer v15. Failing example from their promptpack: 

```
input: \"Invoice total: $9,876,543.21\"
expected: \"$9,876,543.21\"
actual: \"9876543.21 dollars\"
```

lena: Huh. Sounds like token merge around commas and the model switching to verbalized units. Could be a mix of tokenization change + small distribution shift after adapter merge. Any chance the adapter contains special-casing for currency tokens?

maria: Adapter is customer-provided LoRA (caspian-release-0.3), no explicit currency logic. We reproduced locally in our quickpack runner. Summary: 200 prompts, 4 fails, all numeric group separators.

```
quickpack: caspian-release-0.3 + cascade-base-int4-awq
runs: 200
fails: 4 (commas dropped -> unitized)
```

dan: Two quick experiments: 1) re-run with GPTQ recipe to see if it's AWQ-specific; 2) run with fp16 base to confirm adapter content is fine. I can spin them.

maria: I already ran fp16: 200/200 pass. So adapter + base behaves fine in float. That points to quant/token pipeline.

lena: OK. I'll diff the tokenizer outputs between v15(fp16) and v15(int4-awq). If commas are being swallowed or merged into numbers by the AWQ tokenizer rewrite that would explain it. Also check BPE merges.

infra-bot: CI job queued: quickpack-repro/3860000000-repro (matrix: fp16,int4-awq,gptq-4bit)  job-id=112233

maria: Dumped tokenizer tokens for the failing case: 

```
tokenized(fp16): ["Invoice", " ", "total", ":", " ", "$", "9", ",", "876", ",", "543", ".", "21"]
tokenized(int4-awq): ["Invoice", " ", "total", ":", " ", "$", "9876543", ".", "21"]
```

lena: There it is. The AWQ integerizer combined comma-separated groups into a single numeric token. Quick-ish mitigations: 1) small tokenizer pre-split hook for commas between digits for AWQ builds; 2) route currency-heavy requests to fp16 as emergency fallback; 3) add customer regression cases to preserve coverage.

dan: For a cleaner fix we could try forcing BPE merges during quant conversion to respect punctuation boundaries. That might be a longer-running patch to the quantizer. For speed I can try a pre-tokenization regex in the model packager: insert zero-width separator between digit and comma to keep them distinct during BPE.

maria: Good idea. Do we have a precedent for that approach?

lena: We used a similar pre-tokenization step last quarter for thousands separators in EU number formats, it reduced token merges in int8 builds. Created PR then: infra/quant/patches#452. We can reuse pattern but scope to AWQ and tag the adapter client.

infra-bot: PR opened: infra/quant/patches#789  author=lena  title="awq: pre-split comma-digit during tokenization for numeric groups"

maria: I'll add the four failing prompts to tests/caspian_currency_quick.jsonl and mark them as blocking for on-board. Also adding a note in the quickpack YAML to run the numeric-regression checks.

dan: Running the pre-split patch locally now against AWQ build. Command: 

```
./ci/run_quickpack.sh --client caspian --adapter lora/caspian-release-0.3 --base cascade-base --quant awq-4bit --patch pre_split_commas --prompts tests/caspian_currency_quick.jsonl
```

infra-bot: quickpack run complete: job 112233  result: 200/200 pass (pre-split patch applied)  artifacts: s3://redwood-test-results/caspian/3860000000/patch-run.json

maria: Confirmed, pre-split mitigates the failure locally. Next steps: land the small patch behind a feature flag for AWQ-only, publish a canary, and update rollout docs for Caspian.

lena: I'll add the feature flag and a route rule: caspian: if header x-client=caspian and content matches money-regex -> use quant-patch=pre_split_commas. This keeps it scoped.

infra-bot: canary scheduled: canary/caspian-commafix @ 2025-05-12T02:00:00Z  target pool: dedicated-canary-5 

dan: After canary runs we'll monitor telemetry for any side-effects (token counts, latency, and new failure modes). Also run embed-sanity since we saw an embed-shift in a previous customer's run.

maria: Adding monitoring checklist: tokenization-diff alert, money-format correctness (>99.9%), latency delta <3%. Also roll back plan to previous fp16 route if anything spikes.

lena: I'll merge PR to infra with flag gated, and coordinate with product for customer notice.

maria: Thanks everyone. Adding thread to the Caspian onboarding board and closing the quick triage once canary stable.

eval-bot: regression suite updated: tests/caspian_currency_quick.jsonl now contains 4 new blocking tests.

infra-bot: deployment started: canary/caspian-commafix job=112244 logs=https://deploys.redwood.dev/jobs/112244

maria: Will follow up with canary results in this thread.
